prompt_md: 10 friends sit around a round table. Each passes their plate to the left or right neighbor, by coin flip. On average, what percent of them end up with no plate?
prompt_short: Pass plates left or right at random. Share left with no plate?
hint_md: Focus on one person. Who could pass them a plate?
explain_intuition_md: Everyone gives away one plate, so it's tempting to think everyone gets one back. But plates pile up: you end up with nothing exactly when your left neighbor passes left and your right neighbor passes right. That's two coin flips going the wrong way.
explain_math_md: For each person, $$P(\text{no plate}) = \tfrac12\cdot\tfrac12 = 25\%$$ and averages add up person by person.
